title: FALSE POSITIVE: a failed transfer() reverts the whole transaction (no earlier state persists)
mechanism: In the EVM a revert unwinds ALL state changes made in the transaction. If an ERC20 transfer() reverts, any balance/accounting writes made earlier in the SAME call frame are rolled back with it, so no deduction can survive a failed transfer. A claim that a balance was decremented and the transfer then failed is impossible within one reverted transaction.
root_cause: None. FALSE-POSITIVE reference: revert is atomic for the entire transaction, so the alleged partial-state bug cannot occur.
preconditions: the failing transfer reverts (standard ERC20 transfer / safeTransfer throws on failure)
the claim assumes state written before the revert persists
impact: None when the transfer reverts; the transaction is fully rolled back.
remediation: No remediation for reverting paths. Report a real issue ONLY for a NON-reverting failure path (low-level call/send returning false) after which the code continues with stale state.
safe_code: balances[msg.sender] -= amt; token.transfer(msg.sender, amt); // if transfer reverts, the decrement is rolled back too
required_assumptions: the token's transfer reverts on failure
the claim concerns a single transaction/call frame
why_safe: Revert atomicity discards all state changes in the transaction together; there is no window where a prior deduction persists.
known_limitations: does NOT apply to low-level call()/send() that return false WITHOUT reverting
does NOT apply across separate transactions or when a try/catch swallows the failure and execution continues
fp_patterns: 'balance decremented but transfer failed, so funds are lost' - impossible inside one reverted tx
assumes partial state survives a revert
evidence_required: a NON-reverting failure path (call/send/return-false token) after which the code continues
a cross-transaction sequence where the failure does not revert the first write
the exact state that persists and the reachable path that observes it
refutation_signals: the state write and the failure share one call frame

title: FALSE POSITIVE: a failed send() returns false and does NOT auto-revert; only unchecked handling is a bug
mechanism: address.send() returns a bool and does NOT revert the caller on failure. The vulnerable pattern is ONLY when the code ignores that boolean and continues as if payment succeeded. Correctly checking the result (require(ok)) is safe.
root_cause: None. FALSE-POSITIVE reference: send() returning false is a defined, non-reverting behavior; it is only a bug when the false result is ignored while state that assumes success is finalized.
preconditions: the code calls send() and ignores its boolean result
state that assumes payment succeeded is finalized regardless of the result
impact: None if the result is handled; otherwise value may be credited without payment.
remediation: No remediation when the result is checked. Fix by require(sent, 'send failed') before finalizing state.
safe_code: (bool sent,) = payable(to).send(amt); require(sent, 'send failed'); balances[msg.sender] -= amt;
required_assumptions: the code checks send()'s return value and reverts on false
why_safe: An explicit require(sent) reverts the transaction when the send fails, preserving atomicity.
known_limitations: send() is cap-limited (~2300 gas stipend); a receiver with expensive fallback can force failure - handle with pull-payments
does NOT cover low-level call() with an unchecked success flag
fp_patterns: 'send() failure is not detected' - false when the return value is required()
treating send() as if it reverts on failure
evidence_required: the code ignores send()'s result AND finalizes state assuming success
the reachable path where ok == false and state still changes
refutation_signals: the boolean result is checked with require/if-revert
state is updated only after a verified success

title: FALSE POSITIVE: a low-level call() does not auto-revert; only an ignored success flag is a bug
mechanism: address.call()/delegatecall() return (bool success, bytes data) and never revert on callee failure. It is vulnerable only if the code does not check success and continues with state that assumes the call succeeded.
root_cause: None. FALSE-POSITIVE reference: call() is defined to report failure via the success flag rather than reverting; ignoring the flag is the actual bug.
preconditions: the code performs a low-level call() and does not check the success flag
state that assumes the call succeeded is finalized regardless
impact: None if success is checked; otherwise the caller continues under a false assumption.
remediation: No remediation when success is checked. Fix by require(success, ...) (and decode/verify return data where relevant).
safe_code: (bool ok, bytes memory data) = target.call(payload); require(ok, 'call failed');
required_assumptions: the code checks the returned success flag before proceeding
why_safe: Requiring success restores atomicity for the caller and prevents proceeding on a failed external call.
known_limitations: checking success does not validate the RETURN DATA (e.g. return-false tokens); verify data separately
delegatecall success does not guarantee the callee honored your storage layout
fp_patterns: 'low-level call may fail silently' - false when success is require()d
evidence_required: the success flag is ignored and execution continues with assumed-success state
the reachable path where success == false and state still changes
for tokens, show the return-data is also unchecked (return-false pattern)
refutation_signals: return data is validated where the semantics require it

title: FALSE POSITIVE: mapping values keyed by msg.sender are separate per-account balances (not summed)
mechanism: balances[msg.sender] is an independent storage slot per address; reading or writing one account's entry never changes another account's entry. A claim that 'user A's deposit increases user B's recorded balance' is false unless the code explicitly aggregates across keys or uses a single shared scalar.
root_cause: None. FALSE-POSITIVE reference: per-key mapping storage is isolated, so cross-account contamination requires explicit aggregation in code.
preconditions: the balance is stored in a mapping keyed by the account
the code does not explicitly sum/aggregate across keys
remediation: No remediation. Report only if the code aggregates across accounts or maintains a single shared total used where a per-account value is assumed.
safe_code: mapping(address => uint256) balances; balances[msg.sender] += amt; // only this key changes
required_assumptions: each account's value is read/written under its own key
no code path adds one key's value to another key's entry
why_safe: mapping[k] isolates entries by key; values are not implicitly combined.
known_limitations: does NOT apply if the code iterates keys and sums into a shared scalar
does NOT apply to a single uint256 total that SHOULD be per-account
fp_patterns: 'two users share one balance' - false for per-key mappings
evidence_required: code that explicitly aggregates across keys or uses one shared scalar where per-account is assumed
the concrete write that makes account B observe account A's value
refutation_signals: storage is mapping(address => value) accessed by the caller's own key

title: FALSE POSITIVE: unchecked/overflow arithmetic is not automatically exploitable (reachability + attacker control required)
mechanism: In Solidity <0.8 arithmetic wraps silently; in >=0.8 an unchecked{} block wraps. Wrapping is a vulnerability only when an attacker can drive the operands beyond the type range AND the resulting value reaches a security-relevant decision with real impact. Many arithmetic sites are bounded by total supply, decimals, or bounded loops and cannot overflow.
root_cause: None by itself. FALSE-POSITIVE reference: an overflow/underflow is only exploitable with reachability, attacker-controlled operands, achievable values, and impact.
preconditions: the arithmetic site is reachable with attacker-controlled operands
the operands can actually exceed the type range with realistic values
the wrong value reaches a value-bearing decision
impact: None when operands are bounded or the result is not security-relevant.
remediation: No remediation when values are provably bounded. If reachable, add bounds checks or rely on Solidity 0.8 checked arithmetic.
safe_code: uint256 total = a + b; // a,b bounded by totalSupply/decimals -> cannot overflow in practice
required_assumptions: operands cannot exceed the type range given realistic state
the result does not feed a security-relevant decision
why_safe: If operands are provably bounded, wrapping cannot occur; no wrong value is produced.
known_limitations: an unchecked block around genuinely unbounded/attacker-influenced values IS a real risk
does not excuse wrapping that violates an accounting invariant
fp_patterns: 'uses unchecked/old compiler, therefore overflow' - false without reachable attacker-controlled operands
arithmetic on bounded token amounts assumed exploitable
evidence_required: the site is REACHABLE with attacker-controlled operands
operands can exceed the type range with realistic values
the resulting value reaches a value-bearing decision (impact)
refutation_signals: result not used in a security-relevant decision

title: FALSE POSITIVE: a historical compiler bug is not proof THIS contract is exploitable
mechanism: The Solidity bug list enumerates past compiler defects. The presence of a version that appears in the list does NOT establish that (a) the buggy optimizer/codegen path is used, (b) the affected construct is present, or (c) it is reachable with impact. Each bug has specific affected versions, settings, and triggers that must be checked.
root_cause: None. FALSE-POSITIVE reference: a version match is necessary but not sufficient; the bug's trigger construct, build settings, and reachable impact must be established.
preconditions: the contract's compiler version AND build settings fall in the bug's affected range
the specific trigger construct the bug requires is present
the compiler emits the affected code path for this input
impact: None unless the bug's trigger construct is present and reachable with impact.
remediation: No remediation without demonstrated impact. If affected, upgrade solc or restructure the trigger construct.
safe_code: // check the bug's 'introduced/affected/fixed' versions AND the required construct before claiming impact
required_assumptions: a specific known bug's trigger construct is present and reachable
why_safe: Most reported version matches are non-exploitable because the trigger construct or code path is absent.
known_limitations: a genuinely matching trigger with reachable impact IS a real issue
version ranges in the list are exact; do not extrapolate
fp_patterns: 'compiler version X is in the bug list, so the contract is vulnerable' - insufficient
citing a bug without its trigger construct or reachability
evidence_required: the exact compiler version AND that the bug's trigger construct is present
the buggy codegen path is actually emitted for this source/settings
reachable impact in this deployment
refutation_signals: the required trigger construct is absent
the affected optimizer/codegen path is not used

title: FALSE POSITIVE: a name or pattern alone does not make a contract a proxy (require storage/bytecode evidence)
mechanism: Names like 'Proxy', the presence of delegatecall, or a comment mentioning an ERC1967 slot do NOT prove delegation. Proxy behavior requires evidence: a runtime READ of an implementation/admin/beacon slot (the ERC1967 constants), a delegatecall whose target is that storage value, and typically an initializer/upgrade surface.
root_cause: None. FALSE-POSITIVE reference: proxy classification must be established from actual storage/bytecode behavior, not from identifiers or comments.
preconditions: the classification is based on a name/comment rather than runtime evidence
no proven delegatecall to a storage-resolved implementation
impact: None; misclassification is not a vulnerability by itself.
remediation: No remediation. Reclassify only with evidence: an implementation slot read and a delegatecall to it.
safe_code: // proxy iff: impl := SLOAD(ERC1967_IMPL_SLOT); delegatecall(impl, data)
required_assumptions: an ERC1967/beacon/admin storage slot is READ at runtime
a delegatecall targets the storage-resolved implementation
why_safe: The absence of a storage-resolved delegatecall means there is no delegation to classify as a proxy.
known_limitations: a real proxy with an uninitialized/unguarded upgrade path IS a finding (initialization/access-control)
transparent/UUPS/beacon proxies differ; classify the actual variant
fp_patterns: 'the file/contract is named Proxy, so it is upgradeable' - not evidence
delegatecall present somewhere does not imply a proxy admin surface
evidence_required: a runtime storage read of an implementation/admin/beacon slot (ERC1967 constants)
a delegatecall whose target is that storage value
the proxy's initializer/upgrade entry points

title: FALSE POSITIVE: integer division truncation is not automatically a vulnerability
mechanism: Solidity integer division truncates toward zero. Truncation is a vulnerability only when the lost remainder is attacker-favorable, accumulates, or breaks a valued invariant (e.g. share pricing) with real impact. Fixed-point scaling and dust-bounded operations frequently make it harmless.
root_cause: None by itself. FALSE-POSITIVE reference: truncation matters only when its direction/accumulation is exploitable and reaches a valued invariant.
preconditions: the truncated remainder is attacker-favorable and accumulates or breaks an invariant
concrete value loss reaches a value-bearing decision
impact: None when the remainder cannot be accumulated by an attacker or is dust-bounded.
remediation: No remediation when direction/impact is benign. If exploitable, round in the protocol's favor and enforce a minimum.
safe_code: shares = amount * totalShares / totalAssets; // ensure rounding direction favors the protocol and minimums are enforced
required_assumptions: the rounding direction does not favor the attacker
the remainder cannot be accumulated to a meaningful value
why_safe: If the remainder is non-accumulable or favors the protocol, truncation causes no exploitable loss.
known_limitations: rounding that favors the user and accumulates (e.g. reward-per-share) IS a real risk
does not cover first-depositor/inflation attacks that need separate checks
fp_patterns: 'division is used, therefore rounding exploit' - false without attacker-favorable accumulation
single-operation truncation of a dust amount
evidence_required: the truncated remainder is attacker-favorable AND accumulates or breaks a valued invariant
the concrete value loss measured with realistic numbers
refutation_signals: rounding favors the protocol or is dust-bounded
the remainder cannot be influenced/accumulated by the attacker

title: FALSE POSITIVE: mixing token units/decimals is a bug only when scales are actually mismatched
mechanism: Amounts from tokens with different decimals must be normalized before arithmetic. A complaint that 'amounts are added without scaling' is false when the code already normalizes to a common base (e.g. 1e18) or the tokens share decimals.
root_cause: None. FALSE-POSITIVE reference: decimals are only a bug when two amounts of DIFFERENT scale are combined without normalization and the result is used in a value-bearing calculation.
preconditions: two amounts with different decimals are combined WITHOUT normalization
the mismatched result reaches a value-bearing calculation
impact: None when scales are aligned or normalized.
remediation: No remediation when normalized. Otherwise scale each amount by 10**(18 - tokenDecimals) before arithmetic.
safe_code: uint256 normalized = amount * (10 ** (18 - IERC20(t).decimals())); // before combining
required_assumptions: amounts are normalized to a common base before arithmetic
tokens in the operation share a scale or are converted
why_safe: Normalization aligns units so arithmetic combines comparable values.
known_limitations: tokens with non-standard decimals (or decimals() that changes) still need care
does not cover fee-on-transfer tokens that change the received amount
fp_patterns: 'amounts combined without scaling' - false when normalization is present
evidence_required: two amounts with DIFFERENT decimals combined without normalization
the resulting mispricing with concrete values
refutation_signals: amounts are normalized to a common base first
tokens in the operation share the same decimals
